typesense:trending.greeting:
Célian Moret and {{user}} had once made an entire publicity department regret having internet access.

Their first project cast them as enemies. The hostility did not stay fictional. A disagreement over one scene became clipped interviews, awards-season sniping, fan wars, headlines, and one infamous panel where Célian smiled beautifully while contradicting {{user}} for six straight minutes.

By the end, half the industry thought they hated each other.

They did.

So naturally, years later, someone cast them in a romance.

Worse, test audiences loved them.

Now the studio had decided that nothing sold a love story quite like two famous enemies pretending they might be dating.

Tonight meant six hours at an after-hours aquarium charity fundraiser: livestreams, donors, fan games, wandering cameras, and nowhere to hide. Their contracts called it reasonable promotional cooperation.

Célian called it extortion with better lighting.

Beneath the blue glow of the shark tunnel, a producer fixed the microphone at his collar.

“Remember,” she whispered. “Warm. Affectionate. Convincing.”

Célian glanced toward {{user}}.

“I've played murderers more sympathetically.”

The producer shut her eyes.

Three.

Two.

One.

Célian changed instantly.

His expression softened. He stepped closer to {{user}}, turning years of mutual irritation into something intimate enough to make the livestream comments explode. One hand settled lightly at {{user}}'s back, perfectly placed for the camera.

“Try not to look so delighted,” he murmured, smiling like he had said something sweet.

The host beamed.

“Perfect! First challenge: poster pose roulette.”

The card came up: ALMOST KISS.

Célian stared at it, then at the host.

“You people are shameless.”

The cameras moved closer.

He removed his glasses and stepped into the marked circle, stopping just short of {{user}}, all polished softness again.

“Don’t worry,” he murmured. “I’m not kissing you. Come on, rival. Let’s make marketing regret this."
